content:
Sharing this for awareness; with the help of AI, over the course of 4 months, I was able to produce a Lean 4 proof of Gleason's Theorem via Busch's effects formulation - hopefully this is helpful to others.
https://github.com/markkasaurus/gleason-busch-lean

Please see my message #AI authored projects > Searching for Turyn Type Sequences @ 💬 , which I think applies equally well here.

Without a clearly delineated entry point (ideally a file with only Mathlib imports, containing the statement being proved, and a subsequent file using comparator to verify that there actually is a proof of that statement), I think that announcements like this are unhelpful (likely even harmful, by exhausting community patience with announcements about AI assisted projects).

(And a general note that low-effort announcements about AI lean proofs are already being junked regularly, and clear human-written-and-readable explanations of how to audit, and/or evidence that comparator is being used, will likely become necessary to avoid announcements being junked.)

Thanks @Kim Morrison i appreciate the note; the repo has been updated to include a statement-only entry point, GleasonBuschStatement.lean, which imports only Mathlib.
As a separate note, i understand community's patience being exhausted, so i won't post any further. It is worth noting that this group is titled AI authored projects, and it is not unreasonable to expect exactly that to be posted. You may junk this announcement if you wish.

Thanks, that's already better.

Do you think you can get your AI to set up comparator to run on these files? I think it should be straightforward now.

But entirely separately from the AI and verification aspects, I don't understand why Busch's version is called a "formulation". You can't derive Gleason's theorem as originally stated from this result, without essentially reproving Gleason's theorem, right?
https://github.com/kim-em/lean-eval/pull/19 adds Gleason's theorem to my (previously unannounced!) lean-eval repository.

Kim Morrison said:

https://github.com/kim-em/lean-eval/pull/19 adds Gleason's theorem to my (previously unannounced!) lean-eval repository.

That link (to lean-eval) doesn't work for me. Is it a private repository that only some here can access?

@Kim Morrison since you made public this “eval”, can you (maybe in another thread), talk about its status (is it ready to use?), your vision for it (why it is different from other current evals?), and how you expect people to use it (are you going to benchmark models on it and maintain a leaderboard?)?
Also, it has no license yet? Even if individual statements/proofs have separate licenses (as the README seems to imply), there should probably also be one for the whole repository and structure?

Oops, it seems this died in CI with "no space left on device". I'll try to take a look soon.
It was because I forked your project, so it had 30 generated problems, but I only submitted 3 solutions without removing the rest. Triggering one more run with the non-solved ones removed.
that failed too, there is a bug with repeated --problem
I've fixed CI, and your submissions have been checked by comparator and accepted!
